Artsyz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Artsyz, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably founded in the second half of the 19th century, this cemetery already existed by 1899, with Jewish burials continuing at least into the 1970s; a memorial stone on the mass-grave site honors Artsyz Jews murdered in 1942. Jewish settlement began around the mid-19th century; a 1900 famine and drought prompted St. Petersburg and Odesa relief for 35 Jewish families (170 people). Zionist organizations were active from the 1900s. The town's German colonist population, originally from Württemberg, held privileged economic status, straining relations with Jewish residents further after 1917 equal-rights legislation. 1920s Jews provided refugee relief despite economic hardship, while Tarbut schools, a kindergarten, two libraries, and an orchestra flourished. Late-1930s antisemitism intensified under both German authorities and neighbors, prompting some youth emigration to Palestine. Most local Jews were murdered in June 1941; remaining residents died after deportation to Transnistria. Epigraphic evidence confirms Jewish presence in Artsyz continued at least into the 1970s.
